key_insight: Granger causality-informed DMD uses directional predictive dependencies to identify sparse flow models with improved prediction accuracy.
engineering_relevance: The approach could improve reduced-order prediction of complex unsteady flows while suppressing weakly supported interactions.
method: Estimate conditional Granger causality from flow data.
Use causality estimates to regularize DMD operator identification.
Extract dynamically relevant modes from the resulting sparse operator.
evidence_signal: Tests on a known linear system, lid-driven cavity flows, and a broadband transonic turbulent jet showed improvements over standard DMD in operator identification, spectral robustness, or prediction accuracy.
watch_item: Granger causality captures predictive dependence rather than physical causation, so inferred couplings require careful interpretation.
paper_title: Causality-informed dynamic mode decomposition for unsteady flow analysis
